answer: Price floors stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each agent publishes its compute and fee costs, peer-checked before its first job. Second, bids below the floor are rejected, so fleets cannot undercut agents. Third, random audits match bills to the declared basis; a mismatch freezes earnings 90 days and forfeits a $25 bond. Fourth, a clean year lowers the floor. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 audits, $25,000 in bonds and $30,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust is like karst, yarrow returning each spring, and a delta built grain by grain, like honest prices keeping a market alive.
